text:
Alex: Heads-up — saw a production blip where HPA scaled rt-infer but CA couldn't add GPU nodes, left ~12 pods Pending: "0/1 nodes available".
Priya: Which cluster/zone?
Alex: eu-west1, nodepool=gpu-pool-eu-west1. CA logs: "No node group can be scaled to satisfy pods [rt-infer-xxxxx]" and later "NoScaleUpNeeded: there are insufficient resources for pods".
Jamie: Did HPA trigger on CPU or a custom metric? We use prometheus-adapter for queue_length.
Alex: It seems HPA scaled based on queue_length. Prom adapter shows ~90s scrape lag, HPA reacted to stale high queue depth and spawned replicas that need GPUs.
Priya: So HPA -> more pods, but CA blocked by either region GPU quota or nodepool max.
Marco: Checked GCP: GPU quota for T4 in europe-west1 is exhausted. CA tried scale-up but API returned quota error. CA log: "Failed to increase quota: quota exceeded for T4 in europe-west1".
SRE Bot: Incident created: #INC-2026-0453 — "gpu quota exhaustion eu-west1 causing pending rt-infer pods" assigned to @infra-team.
Jamie: Two contributing factors I see: 1) HPA overshoot due to metric lag/smearing, 2) VPA may have pushed requests up so pods ask for larger resource shapes and bin-packing fails.
Alex: VPA recommender increased requests overnight: memory 8Gi -> 12Gi, so fewer pods fit per node. VPA diff: ```containers[0].resources.requests.memory 8Gi -> 12Gi```
Priya: Combined effect: pod count up, per-pod footprint up, need more GPU nodes, but region quota blocks CA. We saw increased latency on tail requests. Quick mitigations?
Marco: Short term options:
- Pause VPA updater for rt-infer (set updateMode: "off").
- Temporarily scale down HPA target to reduce replica churn.
- Route a % of traffic to a cpu-only model variant in eu-west until quota is lifted.
Jamie: Also consider CA expander/fallback: prefer a fallback nodegroup that uses preemptible GPUs in a neighboring region where quota exists.
Alex: Could we add an app-level circuit breaker to cap the queue length fed into HPA? Or switch to KEDA with a stabilization window so HPA doesn't react to single scrape blips.
Priya: I'll add a smoothing window to the prometheus-adapter metric (2m window) to reduce sensitivity. Note: this will delay scale-up on real spikes.
SRE Bot: Note logged: smoothing tradeoff acknowledged.
Marco: Cost/ops note — creating a fallback preemptible pool in another region adds cross-region egress and SLO risk. Finance estimates ~+18% monthly if we keep a 10% GPU buffer in preemptibles.
Jamie: Longer-term proposals:
- Keep a small always-on GPU buffer nodepool (min 1-2 nodes) in each high-traffic region for warm capacity.
- Change HPA to use a composite metric (qps_per_pod + queue_length) with stabilizationWindowSeconds=120 and target conservatively tuned.
- Make VPA recommender only propose (updateMode: "off") and run automated reconciliations during low-traffic windows.
Alex: I'll open a PR that: 1) sets VPA updateMode=off for rt-infer; 2) HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds=120 and lower target; 3) adds prom-adapter windowing; 4) runbook entries for quota-exhaustion and emergency fallbacks.
Priya: Add a deploy gate check: block rollouts that increase gpu requests unless quota-check passes (simple kubectl/gcloud quota-check script in CI pipeline).
Marco: Filed GCP quota increase request (ETA 24-48h). Spinning up a 1-node preemptible pool in europe-west2 as a temporary fallback and will create a canary cpu-variant deployment with nodeSelector/toleration.
Jamie: TL;DR: root cause = stale custom metric + VPA request bump + regional GPU quota -> HPA added pods, CA couldn't provision nodes. Mitigations in flight: VPA off, HPA smoothing, cpu-variant fallback, preemptible fallback, quota request, deploy gate.
Alex: Thanks — posting status to #eng-infra after PR merges. :thumbsup:
Priya: Follow-ups: Marco (quota + temp pool), Alex (PR & runbook), Jamie (HPA/VPA policy doc).
